text:
Dallas had the better of this game by almost any measure except the one that counts. The Stars generated 65 shot attempts to Nashville's 52, held a slight edge in expected goals (2.37 to 2.18), and came out ahead in 54 percent of simulated replays of every shot. They lost 2-1 anyway, because both Nashville goals came on the power play and the Predators spent almost all of their good work in the first period.

The first 20 minutes decided it. Miro Heiskanen scored 47 seconds in, but Nashville answered on a power play when Steven Stamkos snapped one home at 4:46. Nils Hoglander then put the Predators ahead at 15:49 with a deflection on another man advantage, a shot that carried only a 4 percent chance of going in. Nashville out-created Dallas 1.33 to 0.59 in expected goals in the period. After that, Dallas controlled the chances, 0.89 to 0.52 in the second and 0.89 to 0.32 in the third, and at even strength the two teams were nearly level (1.82 to 1.83).

Juuse Saros made the difference after the opening period. Dallas put 30 shots on him and generated 2.37 expected goals, yet got only Heiskanen's early strike, leaving Saros 1.37 goals better than expected. Casey DeSmith was solid at the other end, but he gave up two power-play goals on three Nashville chances with the man advantage, while Dallas went 0 for 1. The Stars took six penalty minutes to Nashville's two, and that discipline gap, more than the run of play, is why the better team left with nothing.
